display.purpose: The h1. One per page, never repeated.

headline.purpose: The h2, always preceded by a hairline rule.

body.purpose: Prose, capped at 46rem for a ~75 character measure.

label.purpose: Uppercase group headings in the sidebar and rail. Nowhere else.

mono.purpose: Commands, tool names, environment variables, JSON, paths.

motion.name: scroll-smooth
motion.purpose: Anchor jumps. Disabled entirely under prefers-reduced-motion, along with all transitions and animations.

components.name: Note
components.description: Something worth knowing before you continue. The label text carries the meaning; colour reinforces it.
components.html:
Note

Everything is created hidden from students. Releasing is a deliberate separate step.
components.css: .ds-note { border: 1px solid var(--rule, #d9ddd9); border-left: 4px solid var(--note, #0a5c7a); background: var(--note-bg, #eef5f8); padding: .8rem 1rem; border-radius: 0 4px 4px 0; color: var(--ink, #1a1c1a); font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; line-height: 1.65; } .ds-note > strong { display: block; font-size: .8125rem; color: var(--note, #0a5c7a); margin-bottom: .25rem; } .ds-note p { font-size: .9375rem; margin: 0; }

components.name: Caution
components.description: Something that will surprise you if you skip it.
components.html:
Importing the same package twice

Two copies of everything. It contains, import into an empty course, or verify there is no overlap first.

components.name: Stop
components.description: Something that destroys data or affects real students.
components.html:
Delete cannot be undone

There is no recovery through this API. Delete previews the object name along with a forum's post count, so you can see what you are about to lose.
components.css: .ds-note-s { border-left-color: var(--stop, #8c1d18); background: var(--stop-bg, #fbeceb); } .ds-note-s > strong { color: var(--stop, #8c1d18); }

components.description: Sidebar and rail links. The current section takes a 2px green left border that is transparent at rest, so nothing shifts when it lights up.

cd lamaku-mcp && pnpm install && pnpm build

components.name: Numbered step
components.description: A CSS counter drives the circle. Used once, for the seven-step course walkthrough. Numbers appear nowhere else on the page.
components.html:
1. Create the modules

    One create_content_module per module. They arrive in creation order.

  2. Upload media before writing pages

    The upload returns the path the page must reference.

components.name: The ledger
components.description: Two facing inventories at equal weight. Nothing may tilt them: no colour on one side, no icons, no counts, no ordering that implies one is the exception.
components.html:
It does

Reads the whole course
Modules, topics, files, assignments, grades, discussions.
Previews every write before it lands
Nothing is written until you spend a single-use token.

It does not

Write quiz questions directly
Brightspace exposes no route for it. Import a cartridge instead.
Write grade values
Untested. The sandbox has no student enrolments.

narrative.overview:
This is documentation for someone who will open it four times a year for five years. It is built to be correct and scanned, not to look current. The bar was set explicitly by MDN, the Django docs, and the PostgreSQL manual: three sites that have survived a decade of taste cycles by never participating in one.

The category default for a developer tool is a marketing homepage with a gradient hero, a feature grid, and a call to action. This system refuses that outright. There is no hero, no pitch, no logo lockup. The first viewport carries the product name, one sentence saying what it is, one paragraph saying what it does, and the install command. A reader who came to install something can start in the first ten seconds.

The one place expression is spent is the accent: Mānoa Green, #024731, the University of Hawaiʻi's own dark green, used for links, the current-section marker, and the focus ring, and nowhere else. It carries maybe two percent of the page's area. Everything around it is white, near-black, and hairline grey, because the accent only reads as a choice when nothing competes with it.
keyCharacteristics: Zero webfonts. The system stack renders instantly and cannot rot when a font host changes.
Light ground by default, with a full dark palette under prefers-color-scheme.
Hairline rules instead of shadows. The system is entirely flat.
Tables and notes are first-class structure, not decoration.
WCAG 2.2 AA verified by script, not assumed.
Two pages, one stylesheet: an overview that persuades and a manual that references. Same world, different composition.

rules.name: The Two Percent Rule
rules.body: Mānoa Green appears on links, the current-section marker, and the focus ring. It is never a background, never a heading colour, never a border on a card. Its rarity is what makes a link obvious.

rules.name: The Verified Contrast Rule
rules.body: No colour pair ships on inspection. contrast.py checks all seventeen pairs across both themes against 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for boundaries. A failing pair is a bug, not a judgement call. This rule already caught the step-marker outline at 1.9:1.

rules.name: The Typed-Things Rule
rules.body: Mono marks anything the reader will type, paste, or see echoed back by a machine: commands, tool names, environment variables, JSON, file paths. It is never used for emphasis, and prose never sets a word in mono for flavour.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, no filter: drop-shadow, no gradient used to fake a light source. If something needs to separate from its surroundings, it gets a hairline and a tonal step.

rules.name: The Equal Column Rule
rules.body: The two inventories on the overview carry the same typographic rank. No colour on one side, no icon set, no count, no ordering that implies one is the exception. Equal weight is the argument the page makes.

dos: Do run contrast.py before shipping any colour change. Seventeen pairs, both themes, 4.5:1 and 3:1.

Do define every colour as a token on bare :root and redefine only the tokens inside @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark). A colour whose only definition lives inside the media query renders one theme's text on the other theme's ground.
Do wrap every table in .tw and give it a caption.
Do put the semantic meaning in the note's label text, not only in its colour.
Do keep new script as progressive enhancement. The page must be fully readable and fully navigable with JavaScript off.
Do render the ʻokina (U+02BB) and kahakō correctly in Lamakū, Hawaiʻi, Mānoa, and JABSOM. This is a brand commitment, not a typographic preference.
Do theme the browser's own surfaces: selection, caret, scrollbar, focus ring.
donts: Don't add a webfont. Not for headings, not for code, not for one accent word. The system stack is the reason this page will look the same in ten years.
Don't add a shadow, a gradient, or a glow.
Don't use Mānoa Green as a background, a heading colour, or a card border. Links, current marker, focus ring, skip link.
Don't put a UH logo, seal, or wordmark on the page. The project is not endorsed by the University of Hawaiʻi or D2L. The author works at UH; the project does not speak for it.
Don't let a heading level skip. h2 to h4 is a bug; the tool-index group labels are h3.grp for exactly this reason.

Don't add a hero, a feature grid, a testimonial, or a call-to-action button, on either page. The manual has no use for them, and the overview answers the same need with the ledger: the honest inventory is the hero.
Don't style the two inventories differently from each other. Equal weight is the argument, and any colour, icon or ordering that favours one side breaks it.
